'''Talitay''', officially the '''Municipality of Talitay''' ([[Maguindanao language|Maguindanaon]]: ''Inged nu Talitay''; [[Iranun language|Iranun]]: ''Inged a Talitay''; {{langx|tl|Bayan ng Talitay}}), is a [[municipality of the Philippines|municipality]] in the [[Philippine Province|province]] of [[Maguindanao del Norte]], [[Philippines]]. According to the 2020 census, it has a population of 17,463 people, making it the least populated municipality in the province.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}} ==History== On July 1, 1996, during the fourth regular session of the second regional assembly of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, the regional legislature created the municipality of Talitay under Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 52 which was approved in a plebescite on June 26, 1999. The town was carved out of the municipality of [[Talayan]].{{cite web|title=Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 52; An Act Creating the Municipality of Talitay in the Province of Maguindanao, Appropriating Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes|url=http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-52.pdf|website=Regional Legislative Assembly, Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao|access-date=27 January 2016}} The ARMM law creating the municipality provides that its administrative center shall be established in [[barangay]] Talitay. On April 15, 2008, during the third regular session of the fifth assembly of the regional legislature, it was then renamed into ''Sultan Sumagka'' through the enactment of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 228.{{cite web|title=Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 228; An Act changing the Name of Municipality of Talitay in the Province of Maguindanao to Municipality of Sultan Sumagka.|url=http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-228.pdf|website=Regional Legislative Assembly, Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao|access-date=27 January 2016}}{{cite web |url=http://armm.gov.ph/armm-content/uploads/2013/03/MMA%20Act%20No.%20228.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2016-06-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083755/http://armm.gov.ph/armm-content/uploads/2013/03/MMA%20Act%20No.%20228.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-04 }} However no record of a plebiscite was held to affirm the renaming. On March 22, 2021, the town was placed under a state of calamity due to family feud (rido) between the former mayor Montasir Sabal and Watamama-Amiril families, belonging to the [[Moro Islamic Liberation Front|MILF]].{{cite news |last1=Punzalan |first1=Noel |title='Rido' displaces 700 families in Maguindanao town |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1135443 |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=Philippine News Agency |date=March 31, 2021}} The former mayor offered his resignation as a result of prolonged fight between the two sides.{{cite news |last1=Fernandez |first1=Edwin |title=Maguindanao guv installs caretaker-mayor opposed by BARMM |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1140588 |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=Philippine News Agency |date=May 18, 2021}} The Maguindanao provincial government installed a care-taker for the municipality, resulting in a controversy with the [[Ministry of the Interior and Local Government (Bangsamoro)|MILG]], considering that by law of succession of the Local Government Code, Moner Sabal should be the successor.{{cite news |last1=Beñez |first1=Rhoderick |title=Bayan sa Maguindanao, may 2 mayor |url=https://www.philstar.com/pilipino-star-ngayon/probinsiya/2021/05/16/2098583/bayan-sa-maguindanao-may-2-mayor |access-date=21 May 2021 |agency=The Philippine Star |date=May 16, 2021}}{{cite news |title=Dalawang mayor sa iisang bayan ng Maguindanao |url=https://ndbcnews.com.ph/news/dalawang-mayor-sa-iisang-bayan-ng-maguindanao |access-date=21 May 2021 |agency=NDBC News |date=May 16, 2021}} On June 17, 2021, the former mayor Montasir Sabal was killed while under police custody after his arrest in the [[Port of Batangas]].{{cite news |last1=Caliwan |first1=Christopher Lloyd |title=Ex-mayor on 'narco list' killed after grabbing escort cop's gun |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1144038 |access-date=17 June 2021 |work=Philippine News Agency |date=June 17, 2021}} When the [[Maguindanao]] province was divided into [[Maguindanao del Sur]] and [[Maguindanao del Norte]] after the [[2022 Maguindanao division plebiscite|September 2022 division plebiscite]], Talitay became part of the latter province.{{cite web|title=Maguindanao Del Norte, Maguindanao Del Sur officially now provinces|url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1666388/maguindanao-del-norte-maguindanao-del-sur-officially-now-provinces|website=Inquirer.net|date=18 September 2022 |access-date=3 October 2022}}
